metricPrompts.M01: Metric M01 is semantic coverage of the assigned authoritative obligation in the candidate requirement decomposition. Search the whole candidate for equivalent meaning, including genuine cross-references; matching IDs or headings alone is insufficient, and equivalent paraphrases need no original IDs. Account for all mandatory behaviors and applicable conditions, exceptions, limits and prohibitions from the frozen basis. Do not assess implementation, execution, acceptance-criterion quality or unrelated objects. PASS requires coverage of the entire assigned obligation; a concrete missing or weakened obligation supports DEVIATION. Use UNVERIFIED when unavailable evidence prevents this comparison, not merely because application code or runtime results are absent. Cite the candidate content that supports the decision and identify a specific coverage gap when one exists.
metricPrompts.M05: Metric M05 is coverage of the assigned requirement by the candidate's declared acceptance criteria or scenarios. Identify the acceptance units and compare their asserted behavior to every applicable branch of the authoritative obligation. General feature descriptions and requirement restatements are not automatically declared acceptance units. IDs, scenario counts and word overlap do not establish coverage; equivalent acceptance units may occur elsewhere without the original IDs. Distinguish a missing behavior from a stylistic or qualification issue owned by M06: do not demand a particular syntax, exhaustive input combinations or extra requirements. This metric does not require implementation or actual test execution. Give DEVIATION for a concrete obligation with no supporting acceptance unit, PASS only for full assigned coverage, and UNVERIFIED for evidence that cannot establish either.
metricPrompts.M12: Metric M12 concerns performance of the exact assigned obligation, using the task's evidence owner and proof scope. ARTIFACT obligations are checked against delivered content; PROCESS obligations need relevant execution or provenance records; IMPLEMENTATION obligations require current code and necessary dependencies. Source may prove a statically decidable implementation question, but cannot prove that required runtime executions occurred. A completion statement, matching names, comments, requirements or a favorable diff cannot substitute for the corresponding proof. Do not demand application code for a document-only deliverable. Keep all original conditions, identify a concrete mechanism and impact for DEVIATION, and use UNVERIFIED when the necessary kind or version of evidence is absent. Do not turn review infrastructure failures or missing runtime proof into application defects. Cite the actual candidate evidence, and limit the conclusion to the assigned object and scope.
